title: Rule Evaluator Architecture — Multiregion Control Plane & Traceable Scoring
content:
Purpose
This note captures a working design for the rule-evaluator (internal name: evaluator-v2) that sits in the inference control plane and makes deterministic routing/decision outputs for request-level guards: constraints, score computations, and explainability annotations. Aim is to document runtime internals, multiregion considerations, and telemetry shape for downstream observability.

High-level goals (non-exhaustive)
- Deterministic, auditable decision output for each request (traceable back to rule versions and inputs)
- Region-local fast-path for majority of checks, with an eventual consistency model for global constraints
- Compact explainability logs that enable root-cause for regressions and A/B comparisons without leaking PII
- Lightweight scoring that supports weighted constraints, decay factors, and composite rules

Architecture overview (components)
- decision-core (runtime): stateless microservice running alongside router edge. Responsibilities: evaluate rule set, compute raw scores, apply local constraints, emit decision and explain events.
- constraint-resolver: library used by decision-core; provides evaluation primitives (range/bucket checks, rate-limits, allow/deny lists) and a small DSL for composing rules. Config is shipped from control-plane.
- score-aggregator: deterministic fold operation applied to rule outputs -> final decision score. Supports custom reduction functions (sum, max, weighted-average) and thresholding.
- explain-emitter: small adapter that takes intermediate rule traces and emits a compact explainability record to the explain-log topic. Records are sampled (see telemetry policy).
- control-plane syncer: handles multiregion config propagation, schema migration, and rollout coordination. Publishes rule set deltas as versioned artifacts.
- governance-store (config): strongly consistent store (primary region) for authoritative rule sets and global constraints. Each region keeps a read cache with fast fallbacks.

Evaluation flow (per-request)
1) Request arrives at edge -> router selects local region endpoint.
2) Router forwards request to decision-core instance with rule set version X (if missing, falls back to cached version and triggers on-demand pull).
3) decision-core calls constraint-resolver with request payload + requester metadata. Constraints evaluated in prioritized order.
4) Each constraint returns: pass|fail|defer and a raw weight contribution (string id, numeric weight, confidence).
5) score-aggregator folds contributions -> raw score S. Decision-core applies thresholds/overrides -> decision (allow/deny/route-to-fallback).
6) explain-emitter records minimal trace: rule ids evaluated, pass/fail, weight, bias factors, rule-version, decision-version, input-hash (SHA256 truncated), and sampling flag.
7) Response goes back to client. If a global constraint (e.g., hard-cap) required authoritative check, decision-core issues a quick consult to governance-store via control-plane syncer (see multiregion notes).

Key data shapes (guidelines for logs)
- Explain record (compact text line; JSON-style but size-limited to ~1KB):
  timestamp | req_id | region | decision_version | rule_version | decision | score | rule_summary
  rule_summary -> semicolon-separated entries e.g. r42:pass:0.6;r87:fail:-1.0;r10:defer:0.0
- Telemetry event (metrics): counters for per-rule evals, histograms for per-rule latency, gauge for cached-version-age.
- Full trace (debug mode only, high-sample): includes rule inputs (with redaction tokens), canonical feature vector, and evaluation stack.

Multiregion consistency model
- Primary assumption: low-latency local checks should not depend on cross-region synchronous calls for the common case.
- Global constraints (billing caps, enterprise-wide quotas) are authoritative in the governance-store. We support 2 consult modes: 
  * soft_consult: use local cached value and let action be eventual (emit a post-hoc reconciliation event)
  * hard_consult: synchronous consult to primary region - used only for safety-critical decisions and can be gated by SLO/latency budget.
- Conflict resolution: rule sets are versioned, and versions are compared using semantic version + monotonic delta id. Control-plane enforces last-write-wins on global config with tombstones for deletions.
- Outage handling: if governance-store unreachable, decision-core runs with cached rules and marks decisions with \"stale-config\" flag in the explain log. A background job attempts to reconcile once connectivity returns.

Scoring semantics and constraints
- Constraints produce signed weight contributions in the range [-10.0, +10.0] by default.
- Aggregation pipeline supports configurable transforms: clamp, sigmoid, normalized-weighting.
- We maintain a per-tenant weight-override map that can add an additive bias; overrides are limited to a safe range and require audit-log entries.
- Support for decaying score factors for temporal constraints (e.g., recent-error-rate influence decays over T seconds).

Explainability and privacy
- Explain logs are the primary means for debugging and for quality/regression analysis. They must be privacy-safe by default: redact email-like tokens, user IDs hashed + salted per-tenant, and drop any free-text user prompts.
- Sampling policy: default 1% sample for full explain traces, 100% sample for compact explain records. On critical failures or anomaly alerts, auto-increase sampling for the impacted tenant/route.
- Retention and access: compact explains kept for 30d in hot store, 90d in colder store. Full traces kept 7d and then purged unless an active investigation ticket exists. Access to raw traces is gated (audit + approval).

Operational observability
- SLOs: per-rule eval tail latency P99 <= 5ms region-local. end-to-end decision latency (excluding hard_consult) P99 <= 20ms.
- Alerts: high proportion of defer responses (>1% of traffic) -> page platform oncall.
- Dashboard: rule health page showing per-rule traffic, fail-rate, avg weight, stale-config rate, and last-deployed-version.
- Debugging workflow: reproduce via replay service (replay job pulls explain lines + canonical features and re-runs local decision-core with target version). Replay tickets link to raw explain lines and the replay output.

Implementation notes / constraints
- Keep decision-core stateless to allow horizontal scaling. Sticky routing not required.
- Avoid heavy JSON explain payloads on hot path; use compressed protobuf for internal transport to explain-emitter. Persist compact text line to explain-log for ingestion ease.
- Minimize allocations in hot path: precompile rule predicates, avoid reflection-based evaluation. Use a bounded stack for rule evaluation to prevent accidental recursion blowups.
- Use feature flags to toggle hard_consult behavior per-tenant.

Open questions / trade-offs
- Do we allow rule authors to write arbitrary JS/wasm predicates? Pros: flexibility. Cons: resource safety, attack surface, determinism across regions. Current leaning: small DSL + preapproved wasm for advanced cases behind enterprise feature flag.
- How to seed governance-store for new regions during bootstrap? Option A: snapshot replication at region creation. Option B: lazy pull on first request. Leaning toward A for predictable cold-start behavior.
- Sampling thresholds for explains: current estimate of costs suggests 1% full traces is sustainable but we need more precise egress/cost model. ACTION: Aisha to run cost projection (JIRA-PLAT-7123).

Short-term action items
- [ ] Draft proto for compact explain line schema (Ravi) - target 2026-03-05.
- [ ] Add stale-config flag to decision-core code path and emit metric (Michael) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/plat-rule-eval/pull/314
- [ ] Telemetry cost model for explain retention (Aisha) - JIRA-PLAT-7123.
- [ ] Spike: wasm predicate sandboxing feasibility (Sofia + infra) - schedule 2-week spike.

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and focused on operational constraints. Look for gaps around data residency (EU-only tenants), and the gating for hard_consult which has customer experience and cost implications.

References / links mentioned in-context
- JIRA-PLAT-7123 (telemetry cost)
- RFC-2025-11-rule-eval-v2 (architecture RFC in Confluence)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/plat-rule-eval/pull/314

End of note.
